Other programs cover lighting and HVAC. Get approval before you buy or install, and check that your contractor is registered.

blocks.x: Heating a building through a Winnipeg winter is expensive, and older commercial buildings can lose a lot of that heat through windows, walls and roofs. The good news: commercial renovations that cut energy use can qualify for Efficiency Manitoba commercial rebates and incentives, which can offset part of the cost.
Here's how to plan energy-efficient commercial renovations, and how to use the incentives available heading into 2027.
Start with a baseline
Before you choose upgrades, know where the energy goes:
**Review 12 to 24 months of utility bills.** Look for seasonal spikes and unusual use.
**Benchmark the building.** [ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager](https://www.energystar.gov/buildings/benchmark) is Canada's national benchmarking tool and can compare your building to similar ones.

**Get an energy assessment** or energy model for larger projects. It can show which upgrades save the most, and it's often part of the incentive process. Efficiency Manitoba's [Commercial Energy Audit Program](https://efficiencymb.ca/business/commercial-energy-audit-program/) covers up to 50% of an audit's cost, but the application must be approved before the on-site work.
The upgrades that matter most in Manitoba
**Building envelope first.** In a cold climate, keeping heat in is usually the place to start:
[Window and door replacement](/services/windows-and-doors)
Air sealing at windows, doors, roof edges and penetrations
Added insulation in roofs and walls during other renovation work

Before insulation or air sealing, review how the work can affect indoor air quality, as [Efficiency Manitoba advises](https://efficiencymb.ca/business/building-envelope/). In larger buildings (Part 3 of the building code), significant envelope alterations can also need an architect or engineer, [the City's commercial alteration guide](https://legacy.winnipeg.ca/ppd/Documents/Permits/CommercialAlterationDesignSummary/Guide-Commercial-Alteration-Design-Summary.pdf) says.
**Then systems:**
High-efficiency heating and ventilation equipment, sized for the improved envelope
Heat recovery ventilation
Building automation and controls
LED lighting with occupancy and daylight sensors
**And water:**
Low-flow fixtures and efficient water heating
How Efficiency Manitoba commercial rebates work

[Efficiency Manitoba](https://efficiencymb.ca/business/) offers programs for commercial, multi-unit residential and industrial buildings, including the **Commercial Deep Energy Retrofit Program**, the Building Envelope Program, the Business Lighting Program and HVAC & Controls.
For [deep retrofits](https://efficiencymb.ca/business/deep-energy-retrofit/), the program:
Supports projects that reduce building energy use by **at least 20%**, using at least two significant measures from different categories
Offers up to **$12,000** toward energy modelling
Pays a performance incentive of **$2.25 to $6.00 per square foot**, scaled to the percentage of energy saved
Adds a 100% bonus on that incentive for multi-unit residential buildings that install a ground source heat pump as the primary heating system, for projects enrolled by **March 31, 2027**
Requires approval **before** any on-site work starts

Projects in this program [generally can't also claim](https://efficiencymb.ca/wp-content/uploads/EM_Commercial-Deep-Energy-Retrofit-Program-Guide.pdf) prescriptive incentives from other Efficiency Manitoba programs for the planned upgrades, so choose your route before you apply.

The [Building Envelope Program](https://efficiencymb.ca/business/building-envelope/) is the closest fit for windows, doors and insulation. Its [incentive details](https://efficiencymb.ca/business/building-envelope/incentive-details/) list these formulas, where U-value is for the whole assembly and lower is better:
**Windows:** $150 x (1.6 - U-value) x window area in square metres
**Curtain wall or storefront:** $200 x (2.0 - U-value) x area in square metres
**Doors with glazing:** $150 for swinging or $200 for sliding, x (1.6 - U-value) x door area in square metres
**Insulation:** up to 7.5 cents x R-value added x area in square feet, depending on where it goes, and no more than the invoiced cost of the insulation materials

Efficiency Manitoba's own example is 20 windows totalling 30 square metres with a U-value of 0.84, for an estimated incentive of $3,420. Products must also meet minimum thermal performance values. The program's pages show different end dates for a temporary bonus on these rates, so ask which applies before you count on it.

The building must be heated mainly with electricity or natural gas, and the project can't have started. Don't buy or install anything until you have approval, and then you have one year to finish. Your contractor must be registered with Efficiency Manitoba, so check its [supplier list](https://efficiencymb.ca/find-a-supplier/) before you apply.
Other programs include:

[Business Lighting Program](https://efficiencymb.ca/business/business-lighting/): eligible LED lamps, fixtures, backlit signs and lighting controls, through a registered supplier, with approval before you buy anything
[HVAC & Controls](https://efficiencymb.ca/business/hvac/): heat pump rebates and variable flow pump and fan systems
[Small Business Program](https://efficiencymb.ca/business/small-business/): free basic products and a free lighting and attic insulation assessment
[In-Suite Energy Efficiency Program](https://efficiencymb.ca/in-suite-energy-efficiency-program/): upgrades to suites in multi-unit residential buildings with four or more suites
Incentives and terms change, so confirm current details at efficiencymb.ca before you finalize scope.

Wait for written approval

Submit documentation for the incentive, which comes after the work is done, so plan to carry the full cost until then
The bottom line
Energy-efficient commercial renovations can lower operating costs for years, and Manitoba incentives can cover part of the cost, as long as you qualify and are approved before you build.
